scenarios.scenario-1: Validation accepts minimal/judgment/binding capsules and rejects unknown programs, unknown keys, shell-like steps, duplicate ids, too many steps and bindings sourced from env.
scenarios.scenario-2: Qualification replays every program through the real child-process path (fake MYGRACE_BIN records argv), records the capsule hash, and `run` then completes with exit 0 and ordered steps.
scenarios.scenario-3: A judgment step returns status waiting with the continue hint and a state file; `continue` resumes and completes; unqualified runs are refused unless --allow-unqualified (warning finding).
scenarios.scenario-4: A failing program deopts with CAPSULE_DEOPT and the source-skill hint (exit 1); a capsule edited between run and continue yields CAPSULE_DRIFT (exit 1); disabled execution or missing required bindings exit 2.
scenarios.scenario-5: The program allowlist is exactly the read-only set (no verify/test/trust/install/diagram writes); capsule list/show/validate work without enabled execution.

required-log-markers.marker-1: No runtime log markers; behavior is asserted through CLI envelopes, state files, qualification records and the recorded child argv.

notes.note-1: Covered by test/grace-capsule.test.ts (17 tests) with a fake MYGRACE_BIN so the suite needs no real project runs.
notes.note-2: Shipped capsules (daily-check, after-change, module-onboarding) are dogfooded manually: qualify on examples/demo-store, run on this repository, judgment/continue and bindings verified.
notes.note-3: Trust model: capsule files are repo input, so run requires a local replay record matching the current sha256; no arbitrary command can be smuggled into a capsule.
